result.api:
RingAssignment (frozen dataclass): rotation: int; per_ring_mw: tuple[float, ...]; total_mw: float; mean_mw_per_ring: float; naive_total_mw: float — result of the barrel-shift optimization, powers in mW.

optimize_ring_assignment(offsets_nm, fsr_nm: float, efficiency_nm_per_mw: float = TUNING_EFFICIENCY_NM_PER_MW, bidirectional: bool = False) -> RingAssignment — enumerates all N barrel shifts of an N-ring bank (ring i serves channel (i+r) mod N), computes h_i(r) = (r*delta - offsets_nm[i]) mod fsr_nm (red-shift-only) or min(x, fsr_nm - x) (bidirectional), P = h/efficiency; returns the minimum-total-power rotation (lowest index on ties) plus the rotation-0 naive total.
result.notes: Design decisions: (1) Discovered and documented a non-obvious tie structure — in the red-shift-only model every rotation total equals fsr*(r + wrap_count) - sum(offsets), so totals across rotations differ only by integer multiples of the FSR and exact ties are generic; docstring notes this and the lowest-rotation-index tie-break. (2) Tests were made tie-robust accordingly: the brute-force property test compares achieved power (not tie-broken rotation index), and the spec's shift-by-1 invariance test uses offsets clustered in one delta bin (where the red-only optimum r=k is provably unique) plus a bidirectional variant with arbitrary seeded offsets. (3) Test suite: 13 tests, all analytic/independently re-derived anchors (hand-computed N=2 red and bidirectional cases, common-mode fsr/2 absorption with exact expected totals and N*delta quantization bound, plain-Python brute-force re-derivation, seeded rngs). result.api: CommonDifferential(mean, sigma_common, sigma_diff, low=None, high=None) — frozen dataclass; value[trial, lane] = mean + common[trial] + diff[trial, lane]; .sample(n_modules, n_lanes, rng) -> (n_modules, n_lanes); optional truncation of the total by resampling (hierarchical: common first, then per-lane diff; exact truncated normal in the sigma_diff=0 limit). ModuleParam = CommonDifferential | Normal | Uniform. run_module(metric, params: dict[str, ModuleParam], n_lanes, n_modules, seed=0, metric_name='metric') -> ModuleYieldResult — metric called per lane as metric(**scalars), ValueError -> NaN lane; Normal/Uniform drawn i.i.d. per lane (dict key must match p.name). ModuleYieldResult: samples (n_modules, n_lanes); n_modules/n_lanes/n_failed; nan-aware mean/std/percentile(p); lane_yield_above/below(spec); module_yield_above/below(spec) = P(all lanes pass, NaN scraps module); report(threshold=None) shows lane vs module yield side by side with the known-good-die gap.
result.notes: Design decisions: (1) CommonDifferential has no name field per spec (params dict keys are names); run_module raises ValueError if a Normal/Uniform's name mismatches its dict key. (2) Truncation of the total is hierarchical (resample common until mean+common is in bounds, then resample offending lanes' diffs) so the shared common mode is preserved; documented that the total's marginal is only exactly truncated-normal when sigma_diff=0. (3) metric takes kwargs in run_module (per spec) vs a dict in run(); documented. (4) Evaluation cost n_modules*n_lanes Python calls, documented. All 10 new tests pass with analytic anchors (p^N independence, exact common-mode equality, lane variance / between-lane covariance, binomial tolerances). result.api: FitResult (frozen dataclass): params dict[str,float], cost, residual_rms_db, success, nfev, message; report() -> str multi-line summary. | fit_transmission(build, params0, wl_um, measured, *, inport=None, outport=None, bounds=None, domain='power_db'|'field_mag', **fixed) -> FitResult — least-squares fit of any component model (ports+s_params) or Circuit (transmission/external_ports) to measured spectra; measured is a single array (inport/outport required) or a dict {(inport,outport): array} for joint multi-path fits (inport/outport must then be omitted). | fit_ring_add_drop(wl_um, through_db, drop_db, x0=None, *, circumference_um, wl0_um=1.55, bounds=None) -> FitResult — joint through+drop fit of RingAddDrop over (kappa1_power, kappa2_power, loss_db_per_cm, neff0, ng) with default bounds (kappas (1e-4,0.9), loss (0,1e3), neff0 (1,4.5), ng (1,8)) and a coarse neff0 pre-scan over one resonance order.
result.notes: Design decisions: (1) chose the dict-measured variant for multi-path fits instead of a separate fit_transmission_multi; (2) circumference_um is a required keyword of fit_ring_add_drop (not in the spec signature) because RingAddDrop cannot be built without it and L is exactly degenerate with neff0/ng — documented as fixed-from-layout; (3) least_squares uses trf with x_scale='jac' so kappas (~1e-2) and indices (~1) converge together; (4) model power floored at 1e-16 (-160 dB) so exact nulls stay finite in dB. Identifiability documented and empirically verified: neff0 modulo wl0/L (coarse pre-scan aligns the comb), ng needs >1 FSR, and — found during validation — (kappa1,kappa2,loss) share a genuinely flat cost valley at 0.05 dB rms noise (identical cost 3.68636 at points ~10% apart), so the fit returns the valley point nearest x0; docstring and example instruct starting from the design asymmetry. Test recovery: kappas/loss within 3-5%, ng within 1%, refit rms within [0.7,1.3]x the injected 0.05 dB floor; multi-seed scatter check showed kappa std ~0.1%, loss std ~0.9% from an asymmetric start. Example runs cleanly without matplotlib (plot skipped with a message, matching other examples' pattern; matplotlib is not a project dependency); PNG was generated via 'uv run --with matplotlib' and verified visually. FdMode: frozen dataclass with neff (float), polarization ('TE'|'TM'), field (real 2D ndarray, dominant E component, indexed [j,i] at (x_um[i], y_um[j]), normalized to max|E|=1), x_um, y_um (1D um coords; x=0 core center, y=0 core bottom).
result.notes: All 5 validation gates pass: (1) slab limit diff -6.8e-4 at dx=0.06; (2) convergence dx 0.03 vs 0.015 delta 1.57e-3 < 2e-3; (3) ordering/bounds ok (TE0=2.70 > TE1=2.22 at width 0.8); (4) EIM comparison at default grid: fd=2.4892 < eim=2.4919, diff 2.7e-3 (sign fd<eim verified numerically, asserted); (5) TE0 mirror correlation = 1.0 (grid is exactly mirror-symmetric; TE1 odd, corr=-1, also tested). Test file runs in ~11 s. Design decisions: (a) an fdmode.py draft already existed untracked in the tree; I kept its Stern discretization (verified correct by 1D re-derivation against analytic slab TE/TM solutions) but changed the meshing: y pitch is now dx_um/4 and both pitches snap DOWN (ceil on cell count) so the core outline lies on cell boundaries — measured O(h^2) error constants were ~2.1 (x) vs ~10.2 (y) per pitch^2, and the original dy=dx_um/2 meshing failed gate 2 (3.16e-3). (b) Honesty caveat documented in the gate-1 test docstring: at width 6.0 the PHYSICAL lateral-confinement shift vs the infinite slab is already -2.9e-3 (> the 2e-3 gate tolerance), so that gate inherently involves partial cancellation with the +2.2e-3 y-discretization error at dx=0.06; a perfectly converged solver would fail gate 1 as literally specified. (c) Semi-vectorial converged limit for 500x220 TE0 is ~2.4881 (Richardson), i.e. above full-vectorial ~2.44 — expected for a semi-vectorial method; module docstring states no polarization coupling, no PML, budgeting-to-design grade.
